name: Eurowhite (1986)
description: All-white fuselage with 'Philippines' in dark bold italics ahead of the wing and a small Philippine flag by the rear door; the fin carries the logo's two sails: a red triangle along the trailing edge and a deep blue one along the leading edge with a yellow sunburst rising from the root, a white band between them widening to the tip. The logo again on the winglets.

sources.note: Branding: the 'Eurowhite' livery by Landor Associates, adopted in 1986; 'Philippines' in italics on the forward fuselage, the logo on the tail and winglets, the flag near the rear.

areas.name: blue sail along the leading edge
yellow sunburst rising from the root into the blue
red sail along the trailing edge

logos.description: The PAL logo on the outer face of each winglet (sharklets, A350 wingtips): a red and a deep blue triangular sail meeting at the bottom with a white wedge between them, a yellow sunburst at the foot of the blue. The fin's art is the same mark enlarged.
The Philippine flag, hoist forward, aft of the rear door below the window line.

titles.style: The PAL wordmark: bold oblique grotesque, capital P, almost black navy, above the windows just aft of the forward door.

notes: Drawn from 2025-2026 photos of A321neos and an A350-1000. The fin art is the same on both sides, blue at the leading edge (mirrored true). The sunburst's ray count is simplified. No belly title: the belly is white. Colors by eye. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on RP-C9930 (right, level): 'Philippines' runs x 0.159 to 0.293, its baseline just above the windows (as drawn), lowercase 0.73 of the P; the flag at x 0.876 as drawn. The fin's sails are straight-edged.
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation. The 1986 'Eurowhite' livery (Landor Associates) replaced the earlier red-white-blue cheatline schemes; minor refreshes since (the title and logo artwork) without changing the layout.
